questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Permutation Given Using Alternate Notation
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for ${}_{n}{P}_{r}$ is given by

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}\,.
$$

$P(15,4)$ means the same thing as ${}_{15}{P}_{4}.$ Using the usual formula for ${}_{n}{P}_{r},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(15,4) & =\frac{15!}{(15-4)!} \\  & =\frac{15!}{11!} \\  & =\frac{15\cdot 14\cdot 13\cdot 12\cdot \cancel{11!}}{\cancel{11!}} \\  & =15\cdot 14\cdot 13\cdot 12 \\  & =32\,760.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group Fewer Than Ten
questions.problem: A store manager is choosing $3$ employees to do the morning, afternoon, and night shifts. If the store has $9$ employees and each can work a single shift, how many ways of choosing the $3$ employees does the manager have?
questions.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $9$ employees to choose from, so $n=9.$ We want to select $3$ of them for the three different shifts, so we have $r=3.$ 

Therefore, the number of different choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{9}{P}_{3} & =\frac{9!}{(9-3)!} \\  & =\frac{9!}{6!} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot \cancel{6!}}{\cancel{6!}} \\  & =9\cdot 8\cdot 7 \\  & =504.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group of at Least Ten
questions.problem: A chocolate box has $15$ different chocolates. In how many ways can $5$ chocolates be eaten in a row?
questions.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $15$ chocolates, so $n=15.$ We want to select $5$ of those chocolates in a row so we have $r=5.$

Therefore, the number of possible choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{15}{P}_{5} & =\frac{15!}{(15-5)!} \\  & =\frac{15!}{10!} \\  & =\frac{15\cdot 14\cdot 13\cdot 12\cdot 11\cdot \cancel{10!}}{\cancel{10!}} \\  & =15\cdot 14\cdot 13\cdot 12\cdot 11 \\  & =360\,360.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group of at Least Ten
questions.problem: Mary has twelve different types of fruits. If she wants to choose three fruits without repetition, one for breakfast, one for lunch, and one for dinner, how many possible permutations of fruits does she have to choose from?
questions.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $12$ pieces of fruit, so $n=12.$ We want to select $3$ of those fruits so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of possible choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{12}{P}_{3} & =\frac{12!}{(12-3)!} \\  & =\frac{12!}{9!} \\  & =\frac{12\cdot 11\cdot 10\cdot \cancel{9!}}{\cancel{9!}} \\  & =12\cdot 11\cdot 10 \\  & =1\,320.\end{aligned}
$$
